transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-24 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood Product), Priya Shah (Novan ML Lead), Tom Reynolds (Novan Infra), Aisha Carter (Novan CTO), Markus Vogel (Novan Data Ops)

Summary (auto): Operationalize precision profiles (INT8/FP8) for LLM inference in clinical workflows. Focus on p95 latency targets, quality thresholds, and rollout plan.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Samir (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intro from our side, I'm Samir, AE, Lina is our solutions engineer, Marcus on product. cause there's a lot to cover I think we'll jump into an Optimize console walkthrough and then show how we'd run a sandbox bench with your prompt set.
[00:18] Priya (Novan): Thanks, Samir. quick context — we're doing triage and summarization over patient notes, strict latency targets for triage (p95 < 350ms) and high fidelity on entities, low hallucination. We're evaluating INT8 and FP8 profiles to save cost but can't sacrifice QA.
[00:37] Lina (SE): Yeah makes total sense. we'll show how Optimize proposes profiles and also fallback rules. side note: sometimes the transcription says I-N-T eight or I N T 8, pardon the jargon.
[00:52] Tom (Infra): Also for us networking: VPC peering, KMS integration, and audit logs are must-haves. on-prem isn't totally off the table but prefer VPC first.
[01:07] Samir: Right — we'll cover Private options and Dedicated as well. quick poll, do you want a short demo of the console first or jump to the benchmark plan?
[01:20] Aisha (CTO): Demo first, then bench plan. want to see the canary/fallback mechanics.

[01:35] Lina: cool. opening Optimize console — this is the Optimize home, you'll see proposal cards. here's a recommended profile for a 7B-type model running on A100-gpu, the default suggests an FP8 sensi-tivity profile labeled "balanced-fp8-v2" and an INT8 candidate called "low-cost-int8-a". the console shows estimated p95 token latency, token cost delta, and a quality delta score based on your eval set if uploaded.
[02:05] Markus (Product): note the quality delta is model-agnostic proxy derived from our evaluation harness — it's not perfect but it flags regressions. you can plug in your own eval to improve fidelity.
[02:21] Priya: when you say quality delta, is that ROUGE or more hallucination-focused metrics?
[02:27] Lina: it's a mix — we compute exact-match on entity spans, a hallucination score from our overlap checks, and an answer-levenshtein/semantic similarity. the dashboard breaks them down.
[02:40] [small crosstalk]
[02:45] Samir: show the timeline — we have Canary stages, auto-fallback to higher precision when quality dips, and traffic split control. in practice you can set thresholds on any metric (entity-precision < 95% triggers fallback).
[03:02] Tom: latency-wise how do you do auto-fallback without spiking cost? if you fallback on a per-request basis won't that double invocation?
[03:12] Lina: good question. our approach is hierarchical: we first attempt the cheaper profile with a micro-time-budget, if the model returns quick and confidence high -> use it. if it times out or fails checks, we re-route to a cached prefix or to a higher-precision model variant. we also use KV cache to avoid double compute for previously-seen prefixes. so you only incur extra cost for fails rather than all requests.
[03:40] Priya: that cache story is interesting — do you share cache across tenants?
[03:45] Marcus: No, dedicated cache per customer in Dedicated/Private deployments. hosted has tenant-level isolation too. cache TTLs are configurable.

[03:58] [05:00] Lina: jumping into a live bench — hypothetical numbers here: baseline fp16 like 1.0x cost, p95 latency 420ms, entity-F1 0.93. FP8 balanced profile shows p95 310ms, cost 0.65x, entity-F1 0.91 (2 point drop). INT8 aggressive shows p95 220ms, cost 0.45x, entity-F1 0.85 (8 point drop).
[05:30] Priya: that 8 point drop would be problematic for us, we need 0.92+ F1 on entities. so FP8 looks promising.
[05:40] Aisha: how consistent is that across longer context? our prompts can be 1.2k-1.5k tokens sometimes.
[05:48] Lina: we instrument by sequence length; FP8 tends to retain fidelity better as sequence grows because representational dynamic range is higher. INT8 can degrade for long sequences — we surface that in the sensitivity heatmap.

[06:10] [07:00] Samir: question for you Priya — what's the acceptable latency SLA? you mentioned p95 < 350ms earlier — is that hard?
[07:10] Priya: hard for triage front-line, some background tasks can be relaxed to 600ms but triage must be tight.
[07:18] Tom: we also have burst patterns; at 10x peak we need graceful degradation. can you show routing policies?
[07:25] Lina: yep. smart routing lets you route by region, cost tier, or latency SLO. during high bursts you can route low-priority background jobs to INT8 pool and keep FP8 for triage. we also support autoscaling with reserved Dedicated capacity and a burst buffer so critical traffic keeps low latency.

[07:55] [09:00] Marcus: talk about metrics to monitor — p50/p95/p99, entity-F1, hallucination-rate, token-cost per request, and model confidence proxy. we recommend synthetic probe traffic during rollout and set canary thresholds.
[09:18] Priya: for canary how long is enough? 3 days, 1k requests?
[09:24] Lina: depends on variance — for you I'd suggest 48-72 hours with stratified sampling across the prompt set plus 5k requests; but the console will compute stability confidence and recommend duration.

[09:40] [11:00] Tom: security — KMS, encryption at rest/in transit, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs — how do those differ across Hosted, Dedicated, Private?
[11:12] Samir: Hosted supports customer-managed KMS (bring your key) in our private tenancy offering, RBAC and SAML SSO, and long-term audit logs as an add-on. Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and tenant isolation. Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you full network control and HSM/KMS integrations; we can map to your SIEM and your SOC processes. we'll send the SOC2 report and architecture diagram.
[11:40] Aisha: good. are logs PII redacted automatically? we need to avoid PHI retention unless explicitly stored.
[11:48] Lina: you can configure retention and redaction rules. for PHI we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with strict retention policies and provide the redaction hooks in the ingest layer.

[12:05] [13:00] Priya: back to the bench: can you run the benchmark on our prompts with our acceptance criteria? also curious about how quantization interacts with certain ops — entity extraction seems sensitive to attention pattern changes.
[13:16] Lina: yes — we'll spin up a sandbox and run an INT8/FP8 sweep. important note: quantization interacts with positional embeddings/scale layers, so we often mark a small subset of layers as higher precision (hybrid-precision) to stabilize entity tasks — Optimize can recommend a hybrid profile.
[13:38] Priya: hybrid profile meaning some layers kept FP16/FP32?
[13:42] Lina: exactly. e.g., keep first 2 transformer blocks at higher precision, quantize others. that reduces the quality delta while keeping cost savings.

[13:55] [15:00] Markus (Product): we also support gradual layer-wise rollouts and zero-downtime switching with model-variant aliasing. you can define a traffic-split that slowly increases share for the quantized variant and set rollback triggers.
[15:12] Tom: what's the expected cost delta if we do a hybrid FP8/FP16 pattern vs full FP16?
[15:18] Lina: typical hybrid FP8 gives ~30-40% cost reduction vs baseline FP16 depending on batch and sequence lengths. full INT8 can be 50-60% but with higher risk as we've discussed.

[15:40] [17:00] Priya: about evaluation — we track entity-F1 but also need to monitor downstream regressions e.g., clinical triage accuracy. can Redwood integrate with our evaluation pipeline?
[17:10] Samir: yes, we can ingest your eval results and map them to console metrics. we can also export event hooks for post-process checks so you can run your downstream metric comparison.
[17:20] [18:00] Lina: demonstration of an actual sensitivity sweep — here's a heatmap showing sensitivity per prompt class. see how certain templates have steep drops with INT8 but are flat with FP8. you can tag templates as "critical" so the rollout keeps them on FP8 or FP16.

[18:32] Priya: would you recommend starting with FP8 for triage and an INT8 pool for low-priority tasks?
[18:40] Marcus: that's a common pattern. start with FP8 for critical paths, run a week-long canary on representative traffic, then optionally add INT8 for background jobs.

[19:00] [20:00] Aisha: can we set per-route RBAC so only certain teams can change fidelity policies?
[20:06] Samir: yes, RBAC at route and model alias level, and audit logs capture policy changes.

[20:30] [22:00] Tom: our infra team needs to run local perf tests; will you provide tooling to run Open-source perf harnesses or do we use Redwood-provided bench?
[22:12] Lina: we provide both. there's a small CLI bench that runs locally against a sandbox endpoint, and a managed Redwood bench that runs in our infra for end-to-end numbers. we'll give you the CLI and a runbook.

[22:40] [24:00] Priya: on hallucinations: any specific mitigations when you quantize?
[24:08] Lina: two lines — model-side: hybrid precision and selective dequantization for attention softmax layers; infra-side: post-filtering checks and rerankers. we also suggested specialized prompts and prefix caching to stabilize outputs.

[24:30] [26:00] Samir: ok let's sketch an operational pilot: goals — maintain entity-F1 >= 0.92, p95 <= 350ms for triage, cost reduction target 25% first month. steps: 1) Novan shares 1k prompt eval set + acceptance criteria; 2) Redwood provisions sandbox and runs INT8/FP8 sweep; 3) Redwood shares results and recommends hybrid profile; 4) If pass, proceed to 72-hour canary with stratified traffic; 5) Monitor and then widen.
[26:38] Priya: that aligns. timeline wise we want pilot running next week if possible.

[27:00] [28:00] Lina: security checklist — we'll include SOC2 report, architecture diagram, KMS integration docs, PII redaction runbook, and tenancy isolation specifics.
[28:18] Tom: good. about logs — can we have event forwarding to our SIEM with redaction applied?
[28:26] Samir: yes, we can forward events and you can configure fields to redact before shipping.

[28:45] [30:00] Priya: any gotchas you've seen when customers go from FP16 straight to INT8?
[30:08] Lina: yeah — sudden drop in structured outputs, tokenization edge-cases, and subtle semantic drift. that's why we prefer staged rollouts and hybrid profiles. also sometimes the quantization toolchain mis-handles layernorm scales — we add compensating calibration steps.

[30:40] [32:00] Marcus: cost modeling — console will show estimated monthly spend, break down by token cost, reserved capacity vs on-demand. for Dedicated we model peak provisioning.
[32:18] Aisha: do you offer commitment discounts for Dedicated?
[32:22] Samir: yes, reserved capacity contracts and term discounts for Dedicated. we'll include pricing tiers in the follow-up.

[32:40] [34:00] Tom: on-prem: if we go on-prem later, how much of this Optimize pipeline can run in our data center?
[34:08] Lina: most of it — the private control plane is pluggable, Optimize recommendations can run locally, and we can integrate your KMS/HSM. the only feature that needs coordination is cross-tenant telemetry to Redwood; that can be disabled.

[34:30] [36:00] Priya: id like to see an example failure case — show a canary that failed and auto-rolled back.
[36:12] Lina: pulling a recent anonymized example — here's a canary where INT8 caused entity-F1 drop below threshold; console detected the drop and the rollout automatically reverted traffic to FP8 variant; audit log shows the trigger and timeframe.
[36:30] [38:00] Samir: wrap up and next steps — we'll provision the sandbox, run the sweep with your prompts, and send pricing/SOC2. any other blockers?
[38:12] Priya: none from ML, just need the eval set and acceptance criteria.
[38:20] Tom: infra needs the sandbox endpoint and network peering details.
[38:25] Aisha: legal wants a sample DPA but that's for later.

[38:40] [40:00] Samir: great. recap of action items and owners in console and I'll email the pilot agreement.
[40:10] [small crosstalk]
[40:30] Marcus: last note — for long term we can instrument downstream KPIs into Optimize so you can track true business impact not just proxy metrics.
[40:45] Priya: love that. thanks all.
[41:00] Aisha: thanks, talk soon.

[41:15] End meeting.

Notes: transcription contains a few mis-hearings (I-N-T spelled out, some product names like "Optimize" as "Optima") typical of call export.
